items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: He had a big studio in his garage. He’d turn the tape on and we’d play all night.

ctx.x: I used to go up and see him, we used to go up and see him, we used to go and hang out for three days.
He had a big studio in his garage. He’d turn the tape on and we’d play all night. He must have tapes that —

My wife — it’s interesting, this was one of the first times I could really show her what was happening. She wanted to come with me and we drove up to Vegas and we went to see Sam, we saw a couple of different shows and everything, and I said, “You’re going to come up and you’re going to hang with us for three days, you’re going to see what we do.” Because anytime, you know, four o’clock in the morning, six o’clock sunrise, you’re walking in after leaving at like six o’clock the night before. “Where do you go?…
